title: Jelly Merge – Free Drop and Merge Puzzle Game
description: Play Jelly Merge free in your browser: drop squishy jelly blobs into the jar, merge matching ones into bigger jellies and float the biggest away as a cloud.
body: A little cloud carries a jelly blob above a glass jar. Move your finger or the mouse to aim, let go, and the jelly drops in with a soft wobble. When two jellies of the same size touch, they squish together into the next size up, with a pop and a happy new face.

There are nine sizes, from a tiny pink drop to a crowned king jelly. Make the king and it puffs into a fluffy cloud that floats out of the jar for big bonus points and room to breathe. Keep the pile below the line at the top of the jar: if a jelly stays above it for two seconds, the run is over. One move, no text, runs of two to five minutes, on phones, tablets, Chromebooks and computers, in portrait or landscape.
New here? Read how to play and the tips for a bigger score.

title: How to Play Jelly Merge – Aim, Drop, Merge and Make a Cloud
description: Jelly Merge rules: move to aim, release to drop, merge two jellies of the same size, make the crowned king to float a cloud away, and keep the pile under the line.
body: Aim and drop: move your finger, or the mouse, left and right: the jelly under the little cloud follows it and a dotted line shows where it will land. Lift your finger, or click, to drop it. On a keyboard, the arrow keys (or A and D) aim and Space drops.
Merge: two jellies of the same size and colour that touch become one jelly of the next size. A merge can push other jellies together, and merges that follow each other quickly score extra.
The sizes: there are nine, shown on the little ladder beside the jar, which lights up as you make bigger ones. The bubble in the corner shows the jelly that comes after the one you are holding.

The cloud: two of the second-biggest jellies make the crowned king jelly. It does not stay: it puffs into a smiling cloud and floats out of the jar, for 160 bonus points, extra coins and lots of free space.
The line: the dashed line at the top of the jar turns orange when the pile gets close and blinks red when a jelly is above it. If one stays above it for two seconds, the run ends.
Coins: every run pays coins (one for every 40 points, plus five for each cloud), and there is a daily gift. Spend them on jelly colour sets and sky themes in the shop.

title: Jelly Merge Tips: How to Make the Cloud and Score Higher
description: Practical tips for Jelly Merge: where to keep the big jellies, how to set up chain merges, how to use the next-jelly bubble and how to make the king jelly float away as a cloud.
body: Big ones in a corner. Pick one bottom corner for your biggest jellies and build the sizes down from there, like a staircase. A big jelly stuck in the middle splits the jar in two.
Keep small jellies together. Small jellies scattered all over the jar are what fills it up. Drop each one next to its twin, or on top of the next size up, never under a big jelly.
Watch the bubble. The jelly in the corner bubble is the one after the one you hold. If the next one matches something, keep that spot free for it.
Set up chains. When a merge makes a jelly next to another of the new size, they merge again at once. Chains score more points in a row, shown in yellow.

Go for the cloud. Two of the second-biggest jellies make the king, and the king floats away as a cloud: the biggest bonus in the game and the best way to empty the jar. Leave room next to your second-biggest jelly for its twin.

Do not rush near the top. When the line turns orange, use small jellies to fill gaps low down rather than stacking higher. A jelly that is still falling never ends the run, only one that stays above the line for two seconds.
Out of room? On some portals, when the run ends you can watch an optional video to clear the jellies at the top of the jar and keep going, once per run.

title: Jelly Merge FAQ
description: Answers about Jelly Merge: is it free, does it save, does it work on phones and Chromebooks, how long is a run, what the cloud does and what the coins are for.
body: Is it free? Yes, it is free to play in the browser, with no download and no sign-up.
How long is a run? Usually two to five minutes. The jar fills a little faster after three minutes, so very long runs come to an end. When a run ends you can play again with one click.
What is the biggest jelly? The crowned king, the ninth size. You never keep it: it turns into a cloud and floats away for bonus points, so the jar gets lighter.

Is it a fruit merge game? It plays like the popular drop-and-merge puzzles, but with our own squishy jelly characters that wobble when they land, a different face for every size, and the cloud that floats away.
Does it save my progress? Yes. Your best score, coins, colour sets and sky themes are stored in your browser (or in your account on portals that offer it).
Does it work on phones and Chromebooks? Yes. It plays with one finger or a mouse, in portrait (the best way on a phone) or landscape.
What are the coins for? Jelly colour sets (candy, pastel, ocean, sunset, neon) and sky themes (day, sunset, candy, night). There are no real-money purchases.
Can I turn the music off? Yes, with the speaker button.

title: Jelly Merge for Schools and Kids – A Calm Puzzle, No Sign-up
description: Jelly Merge is a short, text-free drop-and-merge puzzle that runs on school Chromebooks: no chat, no purchases, no account, a playful way to practise planning, sorting by size and spatial reasoning.
h1: Jelly Merge for classrooms and kids
body: Jelly Merge has no chat, no account, no real-money purchases and no personal data. There is no text to read, only numbers and icons, so it works in any language and for early readers. A run lasts a few minutes and can be stopped at any moment.
It runs in the browser on Chromebooks, tablets and computers with a mouse or a finger, and it is light (a 0.7 MB package including the music).

Every drop is a small exercise in planning ahead: where will this jelly land, what will it touch, and where should the next one go? The size ladder beside the jar turns it into a game about ordering by size and doubling: two of a size make the next one.

It is also a gentle start for talking about space and shapes: round things leave gaps, big things fill corners, and a tidy jar holds more. Ask students to predict which jellies will merge before they drop, then check. There is no violence: when the jar is full, the jellies just look a little worried.
